drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What sexual health concern brings you in: possible STI exposure, a new symptom, contraception, pregnancy worry, pain with sex, or something else?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main sexual health concern guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: Are you currently sexually active, and when was your last sexual contact?
questions.rationale: Recent activity sets the window for testing and post-exposure options.

questions.text: Do you have sex with men, women, or both?
questions.rationale: Partner gender guides which infections and sites to test.

questions.text: How many sexual partners have you had in the past 12 months, and in the past 3 months?
questions.rationale: Partner number estimates STI risk and testing frequency.

questions.text: Have you had a new partner recently, or do you think your partner has other partners?
questions.rationale: New or concurrent partners raise STI risk.

questions.text: What kinds of sex have you had: vaginal, anal, or oral?
questions.rationale: Types of sex determine which body sites need STI testing.

questions.text: How often do you use condoms or other barriers: always, sometimes, or never?
questions.rationale: Barrier use modifies STI and HIV risk.

questions.text: In the past 72 hours, have you had sex without a condom with someone who has HIV or whose status you do not know, or had a condom break?
questions.rationale: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis works best when started within 72 hours.

questions.text: Has a partner told you they have an STI, HIV, or hepatitis?
questions.rationale: A partner's diagnosis warrants testing and often presumptive treatment.

questions.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with an STI such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, herpes, or HIV?
questions.rationale: Past STIs raise the likelihood of current infection.

questions.text: When were you last tested for STIs and HIV, and what were the results?
questions.rationale: Testing history sets what screening is now due.

questions.text: Do you have discharge, burning, itching, sores, bumps, or a rash in the genital or anal area?
questions.rationale: Genital symptoms guide examination and testing.

questions.text: Do you have a genital sore along with fever, a body rash, swollen glands, or joint pain?
questions.rationale: Systemic symptoms with ulcers suggest secondary syphilis, primary HIV, or disseminated gonorrhea.

questions.text: Do you have lower belly or pelvic pain, pain with sex, or fever?
questions.rationale: Pelvic pain with fever raises concern for pelvic inflammatory disease.

questions.text: Do you have pain or swelling in a testicle?
questions.rationale: Testicular pain can be epididymitis or torsion, which is an emergency.

questions.text: Are you using any birth control now, and is it working for you?
questions.rationale: Contraceptive use guides pregnancy risk and counseling.

questions.text: When was your last period, and is it possible you are pregnant?
questions.rationale: Possible pregnancy changes testing, treatment choices, and urgency.

questions.text: Have you heard of or used PrEP, a daily or injectable medicine that prevents HIV?
questions.rationale: Eligible patients benefit from HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis.

questions.text: Have you been vaccinated against HPV, hepatitis B, hepatitis A, and mpox?
questions.rationale: Vaccination prevents several sexually transmitted infections.

questions.text: Have you ever exchanged sex for money, drugs, housing, or other needs?
questions.rationale: Transactional sex raises STI risk and can indicate exploitation.

questions.text: Do you use alcohol or drugs before or during sex?
questions.rationale: Substance use with sex is linked to condomless sex and assault.

questions.text: Has anyone ever forced or pressured you into sexual contact you did not want, or did something happen recently?
questions.rationale: Recent assault needs urgent care, evidence collection options, and prophylaxis.

questions.text: Do you have any concerns with desire, arousal, erections, orgasm, or pain during sex?
questions.rationale: Sexual dysfunction is common and may signal medical or medication causes.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Recent sexual assault
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe being forced or pressured into sexual contact, especially within the last few days?

red_flags.label: Possible HIV exposure within 72 hours
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report condomless sex, a broken condom, or needle sharing with a partner of positive or unknown HIV status within the last 72 hours?

red_flags.label: Pelvic pain with fever
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report lower abdominal or pelvic pain with fever, pain during sex, or abnormal discharge?

red_flags.label: Testicular pain or swelling
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report sudden or severe testicular pain or swelling?

red_flags.label: Genital sore with systemic symptoms
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a genital sore or rash together with fever, body rash, swollen glands, or joint pain?

red_flags.label: Possible pregnancy with pain or bleeding
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a missed or late period together with pelvic pain or vaginal bleeding?
